rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When” can modify Abraham or his earlier description, or attach to “was,” with an intervening parenthesis; the vocative ta replaces possessive ya, and repetition conveys tenderness.
rows.anchor: { إذ قال } بدل من { إبراهيم } وما بينهما اعتراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols cannot perceive their worshipper, hear or see him, or bring benefit or avert harm. Abraham argues gently for worship of the self-sufficient creator alone; even contingent angels and prophets are not worthy of worship, much less inanimate idols.
rows.anchor: لا تحق إلا لمن له الاستغناء التام والإنعام العام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sound reason requires purposeful action; Abraham invites his father to follow him toward the straight path because he has received knowledge his father lacks.
rows.anchor: فكيف إذا كان جمادا لا يسمع ولا يبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham tactfully presents himself as a fellow traveler more familiar with the route instead of insulting his father’s ignorance or boasting of superior knowledge.
rows.anchor: جعل نفسه كرفيق له في مسير يكون أعرف بالطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idol worship is effectively worship of Satan because he commands it; Satan disobeys the Lord who bestowed every blessing, and an obedient follower shares the rebel’s fault.
rows.anchor: مستعص على ربك المولي للنعم كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s ally either accompanies him in curse and punishment or persists in allegiance, which is worse than punishment; fear, touch, and indefinite punishment soften the warning or reflect uncertainty.
rows.anchor: قرينا في اللعن والعذاب تليه ويليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham singles out Satan’s disobedience because of his own spiritual aspiration, because rebellion is its root, or because it signals Satan’s enmity to Adam’s descendants.
rows.anchor: ولعل اقتصاره على عصيان الشيطان من بين جناياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The father answers tenderness with harshness, calls Abraham by name rather than “my son,” and uses an interrogative to express astonished rejection; the threat may mean insult, stoning, or expulsion.
rows.anchor: قابل استعطافه ولطفه في الارشاد بالفظاظة وغلظة العناد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A long while” can mean a long time or going far away.
rows.anchor: زمانا طويلا من الملاوة أو مليا بالذهاب عني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham’s peace is farewell and separation, answering injury with kindness; seeking forgiveness for an unbeliever means asking God to guide him to repentance and faith.
rows.anchor: توديع ومتاركة ومقابلة للسيئة بالحسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God was abundantly benevolent and gracious to Abraham.
rows.anchor: بليغا في البر والإلطاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham migrates for his faith and worships God alone; “perhaps” expresses humility, recognizes that prayer and reward are gifts rather than obligations, and acknowledges the unseen outcome.
rows.anchor: { وأعتزلكم وما تدعون من دون الله } بالمهاجرة بديني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Abraham migrated to Syria, God gave him Isaac and Jacob in place of the unbelievers he left. It is said he first reached Harran and married Sarah; the two may be singled out as prophetic lineages, while Ishmael is mentioned separately.
rows.anchor: { وهبنا له إسحق ويعقوب } بدل من فارقهم من الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Both” refers either to Isaac and Jacob or to the sons collectively.
rows.anchor: وكلا منهما أو منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mercy granted to the family comprises prophethood, wealth, and children. Their elevated reputation answers Abraham’s prayer for a good name among later generations; tongue means the instrument of speech, and their praise endures across eras and religions.
rows.anchor: النبوة والأموال والأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was devoted to monotheism and worship free from shirk and ostentation, or submitted wholly to God; the Kufans read with fatḥa, making God the one who chose him.
rows.anchor: موحدا أخلص عبادته عن الشرك والرياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Messenger” precedes “prophet” because God sent Moses to people so he could inform them about Him.
rows.anchor: أرسله الله إلى الخلق فأنبأهم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The right side is the mountain’s right side or Moses’s right as he faced it; the blessed side also suggests speech was represented from there. Drawing Moses near is honor like a king’s private audience.
rows.anchor: من ناحيته اليمنى من اليمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In intimate conversation” is circumstantial, or can mean raised from the word for high ground; a report says Moses was raised above the heavens until hearing the pen creak.
rows.anchor: لما روي أنه رفع فوق السموات حتى سمع صرير القلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron was granted as mercy or a portion of mercy to support Moses, answering his request for a helper from his family; Aaron was older than Moses.
rows.anchor: من أجل رحمتنا أو بعض رحمتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “His brother” is an object or appositive if “from” is partitive; Aaron specifies brother and “prophet” is circumstantial.
rows.anchor: فإنه كان أسن من موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael is renowned for keeping promises and fulfilled his promise to endure the sacrifice; calling him messenger and prophet shows that a messenger need not bring a new law, since Abraham’s descendants followed his law.
rows.anchor: ذكره بذلك لأنه المشهور به والموصوف بأشياء في هذا الباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ishmael first improved himself and those nearest him, as other verses command warning one’s kin and caring for one’s household; “family” may mean his community, since prophets are fathers to communities.
rows.anchor: اشتغالا بالأهم وهو أن يقبل الرجل على نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He was pleasing to his Lord because his words and actions were upright.
rows.anchor: لاستقامة أقواله وأفعاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idris descended from Seth and preceded Noah; his name was Akhnukh. Deriving Idris from study is challenged by its diptote form, though it may have a similar meaning in his language and refer to his frequent study.
rows.anchor: وهو سبط شيث وجد أبي نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports say God sent Idris thirty scriptures, that he first wrote with a pen, and that he studied astronomy and calculation.
rows.anchor: أنه تعالى أنزل عليه ثلاثين صحيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idris’s exalted station means the honor of prophethood and nearness to God.
rows.anchor: يعني شرف النبوة والزلفى عند الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other interpretations identify the station as Paradise, the sixth heaven, or the fourth.
rows.anchor: وقيل الجنة. وقيل السماء السادسة أو الرابعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those” refers to the prophets from Zechariah through Idris, favored with religious and worldly blessings; “from Adam’s descendants” may be an appositive or partitive.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى المذكورين في السورة من زكريا إلى إدريس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those carried with Noah means their descendants other than Idris; Abraham descended from Shem. Moses, Aaron, Zechariah, John, and Jesus descend from Israel, proving daughters’ children count as descendants.
rows.anchor: ومن ذرية من حملنا خصوصا، وهم من عدا إدريس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were guided to truth and chosen for prophethood and honor; prostration and weeping show reverence despite their noble lineage. The Prophet urged Quran recitation and weeping or feigned weeping; readings vary in the verb and bāʾ vowel.
rows.anchor: اتلوا القرآن وابكوا فإن لم تبكو فتباكوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A bad successor followed the righteous; khalaf with fatḥa can mean good successor, sukūn bad. Neglecting prayer means abandoning or delaying it; desires include wine, permitting a paternal half-sister, and other sins.
rows.anchor: فعقبهم وجاء بعدهم عقب سوء يقال خلف صدق بالفتح

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali describes followers of desire as those who build ostentatiously, ride showily, and wear conspicuous clothes.
rows.anchor: من بنى الشديد، وركب المنظور، ولبس المشهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghayy can mean evil, the recompense for misguidance, deviation from Paradise’s path, or a valley in Hell; the source cites a poem and another verse.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو واد في جهنم يستعيذ منه أوديتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception indicates that the preceding verses concern unbelievers; several readers use the passive “they will be entered.” The repentant lose none of their recompense, and past disbelief does not diminish reward.
rows.anchor: يدل على أن الآي في الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Abu Amr, Abu Bakr, and Yaqub read the verb passively.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وأبو بكر ويعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gardens of Eden is an appositive naming part of Paradise or an expression of praise; Eden means enduring residence or is a proper name. Paradise is promised unseen, and its promise will certainly be fulfilled.
rows.anchor: بدل من الجنة بدل البعض لاشتمالها عليها، أو منصوب على المدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Peace” may be sound speech, greetings from angels or one another, or a courteous salutation; alternatively it is the sole exception to idle talk, as in the cited poem. Morning and evening provision reflects custom and balance, or continual provision.
rows.anchor: ولكن يسمعون قولا يسلمون فيه من العيب والنقيصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God leaves Paradise to the righteous as the fruit of piety; inheritance conveys lasting secure possession. Alternatively, they inherit the dwellings that would have belonged to the people of Hell, and Yaqub reads with doubled rāʾ.
rows.anchor: نبقيها عليهم من ثمرة تقواهم كما يبقى على الوارث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel says this to Muhammad after delayed revelation about the Cave companions, Dhul-Qarnayn, and the Spirit; the delay was fifteen or forty days and unbelievers said God had abandoned him.
rows.anchor: حكاية قول جبريل عليه الصلاة والسلام حين استبطأه رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels descend gradually or generally only by God’s wise command; all places and times belong to Him, and delayed revelation was not abandonment. Alternatively, the pious say this on entering Paradise, affirming God has not forgotten their deeds or promised reward.
rows.anchor: لا ننتقل من مكان إلى مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Lord of the heavens” explains why God cannot forget; it is a predicate of an omitted subject or appositive. The Prophet should worship and persevere through hardship, delayed revelation, and mockery.
rows.anchor: بيان لامتناع النسيان عليه، وهو خبر محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Namesake means a peer deserving divinity or anyone named Allah; idolaters call idols gods but never Allah. Since none resembles God or deserves worship, one must submit and serve Him.
rows.anchor: مثلا يستحق أن يسمى إلها أو أحدا سمي الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The human” may mean humankind collectively or specific unbelievers, including Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who crumbled bones and challenged resurrection. The disputed life is emergence from earth or return from death; syntax emphasizes postmortem timing.
rows.anchor: أو أبي بن خلف فإنه أخذ عظاما بالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām emphasizes futurity and prevents the future verb from governing backward; Ibn Dhakwan is reported to read one hamza with kasra as a statement.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن ذكوان إذا ما مت بهمزة واحدة مكسورة على الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question coordinates with “he says”; its placement stresses that resurrection denial is the main target. Remembering creation from nothing would remove doubt, since reassembly is less wondrous.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على أن المنكر بالذات هو المعطوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi, Ibn Amir, Asim, and Qalun from Yaqub read “remember/reflect”; another reading keeps the original form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر وعاصم وقالون عن يعقوب { يذكر }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath joins God’s name to His Prophet to confirm the event and magnify the Messenger. A report says unbelievers are chained to their devil companions.
rows.anchor: أقسم باسمه تعالى مضافا إلى نبيه تحقيقا للأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saved see what they escaped and rejoice; the damned see their fate and envy their departure. Kneeling stems from terror or waiting for judgment, as another verse depicts; unbelievers may also be led kneeling in humiliation or exhaustion.
rows.anchor: لما يدهمهم من هول المطلع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sect is a community united by religion; extracting the most rebellious first signals that God forgives many sinners. If only unbelievers are meant, He ranks each sect and assigns fitting levels.
rows.anchor: من كل أمة شاعت دينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sibawayh builds “which of them” on ḍamma like relatives, with accusative position; other parses make it an interrogative subject, a reported question, or a suspended question because extraction entails distinction.
rows.anchor: مبني على الضم عند سيبويه لأن حقه أن يبنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parses attach it to “sect,” meaning those who follow, or treat the particle as explanatory or additional.
rows.anchor: وإما بشيعة لأنها بمعنى تشيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those most entitled to burn are the extracted rebels, or the leaders of sects, whose punishment is doubled for misguiding others.
rows.anchor: وهم المنتزعون ويجوز أن يراد بهم وبأشدهم عتيا رؤساء الشيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read the ṣād with kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص { صليا } بكسر الصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Among you” shifts address to humankind and supports “among them”; arrival means reaching Hell, where believers pass while it is extinguished and others fall in. Alternatively it means crossing the bridge over it.
rows.anchor: وما منكم التفات إلى الإنسان ويؤيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a report from Jabir, the Prophet says believers in Paradise will be told they approached the Fire while it was extinguished.
rows.anchor: وعن جابر رضي الله عنه أن رسول الله عليه الصلاة والسلام سئل عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being kept far from Hell means being kept from its punishment; God made the approach binding by an irrevocable promise, or swore to it.
rows.anchor: كان ورودهم واجبا أوجبه الله على نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God leads the God-fearing to Paradise; al-Kisāʾī and Yaqub read without doubling, and another reading opens the thāʾ. The sinners’ remaining kneeling supports their separation after the righteous depart.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي ويعقوب ننجي بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are clear in wording, meaning, and inimitability; “better station” means a place to stand or reside, with Ibn Kathir reading residence, while assembly means gathering.
rows.anchor: مرتلات الألفاظ مبينات المعاني بنفسها أو ببيان الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unable to challenge revelation, unbelievers boast of worldly advantages as proof of merit; the passage answers and threatens them.
rows.anchor: أخذوا في الافتخار بما لهم من حظوظ الدنيا والاستدلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “How many” is the object of “destroyed,” and “generations” explains it; a generation is named for the animal’s leading horn. Household goods are furnishings, perhaps specifically new possessions; appearance derives from seeing.
rows.anchor: وإنما سمي أهل كل عصر قرنا أي مقدما من قرن الدابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Readings change, invert, or omit the hamza, or give “zayyā,” a collection of beauties; worldly enjoyment is entrapment rather than honor.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن عامر «ريا» على قلب الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those astray receive longer lives and enjoyment as entrapment and to cut off excuses; “until they see” ends the respite or their boast. The outcome is worldly defeat or the Hour, exposing their worse position and weaker support.
rows.anchor: فيمده ويمهله بطول العمر والتمتع به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God increases the guided in guidance, showing believers’ smaller worldly share is not inferiority but provision for something better; alternatively the clause coordinates with respite and contrasts increased misguidance.
rows.anchor: قصور حظ المؤمن منها ليس لنقصه بل لأن الله عز وجل أراد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lasting good works include the five prayers and praises of God; unlike ephemeral worldly favors, their return is everlasting bliss. “Better” may mean greater or be a comparative expression.
rows.anchor: الطاعات التي تبقى عائدتها أبد الآباد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Revealed about al-As ibn Waʾil, who owed Khabbab money and refused payment until he disbelieved, then claimed future wealth and children after resurrection. “Have you seen?” means report; access to the unseen or a divine covenant are the only possible bases for the claim.
rows.anchor: نزلت في العاص بن وائل كان لخباب عليه مال فتقاضاه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The covenant may mean testimony of faith and righteous action, for God’s reward-promise resembles a covenant.
rows.anchor: وقيل العهد كلمة الشهادة والعمل الصالح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisāʾī read the word for children as a plural or dialect variant.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «ولدا» وهو جمع ولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No” rebukes his mistaken self-image; God will expose his recorded words or exact retribution as for a recorded crime. Punishment will be prolonged or doubled for disbelief and mockery.
rows.anchor: ردع وتنبيه على أنه مخطىء فيما تصوره لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inherits his wealth and children at death; he comes alone without them, or alone after abandoning his claim.
rows.anchor: { فردا } لا يصحبه مال ولا ولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idolaters take gods to gain strength, treating them as a connection to God and intercessors.
rows.anchor: ليتعززوا بهم حيث يكونون لهم وصلة إلى الله وشفعاء عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols may disavow their worshippers, or the unbelievers may deny worshipping them; the idols become disgrace, fuel for their fire, or objects of disbelief, opposing former worshippers.
rows.anchor: ستجحد الآلهة عبادتهم ويقولون ما عبدتمونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse is read with nunation at the pause; this may be a sound change or an elliptical construction. The saying calls believers one hand against others.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { كلا } بالتنوين على قلب الألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God empowered devils over unbelievers or appointed them companions; they incite sins through seductive suggestions and desires, prompting wonder at their obstinacy despite clear proof.
rows.anchor: تهزهم وتغريهم على المعاصي بالتسويلات وتحبيب الشهوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet should not hurry their destruction; God is counting their finite days and breaths, so only a short time remains.
rows.anchor: أيام آجالهم. { عدا } والمعنى لا تعجل بهلاكهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gathers the God-fearing to the Lord who envelops them in mercy; this divine name suits the surah’s account of blessings and gratitude or rejection. They arrive as honored delegates expecting generosity.
rows.anchor: إلى ربهم الذي غمرهم برحمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Criminals are driven like livestock, thirsty as animals going to water, or simply like beasts herded to a watering place.
rows.anchor: كما تساق البهائم. { إلى جهنم وردا } عطاشا فإن من يرد الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to all servants inferred from the two groups. A covenant may mean faith and good works qualifying one to intercede or explicit divine permission; alternatively it is the criminals who may be interceded for by a Muslim.
rows.anchor: إلا من تحلى بما يستعد به ويستأهل أن يشفع للعصاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may be nominative apposition, accusative with an omitted noun meaning intercession, or direct exception.
rows.anchor: ومحله الرفع على البدل من الضمير أو النصب على تقدير مضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun may refer to either group, since a statement circulated among people may be attributed to them collectively.
rows.anchor: لأن هذا لما كان مقولا فيما بين الناس جاز أن ينسب إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct address shifts perspective to intensify blame and mark audacity; related forms of idd convey a grave, outrageous matter or severity and heaviness.
rows.anchor: على الالتفات للمبالغة في الذم والتسجيل عليهم بالجراءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nafi and al-Kisāʾī read with a feminine yāʾ; other named readers read “split apart,” while the first form is more emphatic.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة وأبو بكر ويعقوب «ينفطرن»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains collapse crushed; the claim is so dreadful it would shatter the cosmos if given perceptible form, or provoke divine anger enough to destroy it were God not forbearing.
rows.anchor: أن هول هذه الكلمة وعظمها بحيث لو تصورت بصورة محسوسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about claiming a child may be accusative as cause, genitive with an understood preposition, appositive to a pronoun, predicate of an omitted clause, or subject of “collapse”; it can mean naming or attributing lineage.
rows.anchor: يحتمل النصب على العلة ل { تكاد } أو ل { هدا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A child is neither fitting nor conceivable for the Merciful; this attribute stresses that everything else receives His blessings and cannot be His kindred.
rows.anchor: ولا يليق به اتخاذ الولد ولا يتطلب له لو طلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made the Quran easy in Muhammad’s language; the bāʾ can mean “in” or retain its ordinary sense because the verb implies sending down. The warning addresses contentious people who pursue every line of dispute.
rows.anchor: والباء بمعنى على أو على أصله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The destruction of earlier generations warns unbelievers and emboldens the Messenger; “sense” asks if any can be perceived. Hidden sound means a faint voice, with a root suggesting concealment.
rows.anchor: تخويف للكفرة وتجسير للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم على إنذارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet promises ten good deeds to whoever recites Maryam for each person who disbelieved in or affirmed the named prophets and each person who prayed or did not pray to God.
rows.anchor: من قرأ سورة مريم أعطي عشر حسنات بعدد من كذب زكريا
